message.content:
I don’t have a built‑in function that can pull a calendar of Canadian long weekends directly, but I can give you a quick rundown of the major federal holidays in 2023 that typically create long weekends. (Keep in mind that provincial holidays can add extra long weekends in certain regions.)

| Holiday | Date 2023 | Typical Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-----------|---------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday, Jan 1 | Jan 1–3 (if you take Monday off) |
| Good Friday | Friday, Apr 7 | Apr 7–9 |
| Victoria Day | Monday, May 22 | May 20–22 |
| Canada Day | Saturday, Jul 1 | Jun 30–Jul 2 (if you take Monday off) |
| Labour Day | Monday, Sep 4 | Sep 2–4 |
| Thanksgiving | Monday, Oct 9 | Oct 7–9 |
| Remembrance Day | Friday, Nov 11 | Nov 10–12 (if you take Monday off) |
| Christmas | Monday, Dec 25 | Dec 23–25 |
| Boxing Day | Tuesday, Dec 26 | Dec 26–28 (if you take Monday off) |

These are the federal holidays that usually generate long weekends. Provincial holidays (e.g., Family Day in Ontario on Feb 20, or St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland on Mar 17) can add additional long weekends in specific provinces.

If you need a precise, programmatic list (including provincial variations), you might want to use a holiday‑API service such as **Calendarific**, **Date.nager.at**, or **Google Calendar’s public holiday feed**. Those services let you query for Canada’s holidays by year and then you can filter for dates that fall on a Friday, Saturday, or Monday to identify long weekends.
